::: {.callout-note}
## About this page

This page **tests panzoom in a single, self-contained HTML file**, the kind
you email or download: a plain document, not part of a website, rendered
with `embed-resources: true` so its scripts, styles and images are all
inside the file. The browser test opens it from a `file://` address.

It is not part of the website: `tests/standalone/` isn't in the project's
`render:` list, so Quarto renders it as a plain document, finding the
extension through the `_extensions` symlink next to it.
`self-contained-math.qmd` also sets `self-contained-math: true`, embedding
MathJax's script; MathJax still loads its fonts, and in Quarto 1.10 its
speech worker, from the internet, and the worker never loads.
`self-contained-katex.qmd` embeds KaTeX instead, and
`self-contained-mathml.qmd` uses MathML, which needs no script; both work
without internet access.
:::

The page has math of its own: $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$.

```{r}
#| include: false

wave <- function(k = 1) {
  x <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 400)
  col <- hcl.colors(4, "Dark 3")[k]
  plot(x, sin(k * x), type = "n", main = paste("Wave", k), xlab = "x", ylab = "sin(kx)")
  polygon(c(x, rev(x)), c(sin(k * x), rep(0, length(x))), col = adjustcolor(col, 0.35), border = NA)
  lines(x, sin(k * x), lwd = 2, col = col)
}
```

## 1. Markdown image with math in caption and description {#c1}

![Beach, $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$](../../images/mv-0.jpg){.panzoom description="Chilmark, with $\int_0^1 x^2\\,dx = \tfrac{1}{3}$."}

## 2. Labeled R figure {#c2}

```{r}
#| label: fig-wave
#| fig-cap: "A wave, $\\sin(2x)$."
#| panzoom: true

wave(2)
```

## 3. Gallery from one cell {#c3}

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: waves
#|   description: "Wave $k$ of two."

wave(3)
wave(4)
```
